rubric_items.reason: The new flipping-clock test now covers REQ-10, plus selection, boundary, closed statuses, list agreement, POST/PATCH, 404 and every web behaviour. One gap remains: the API never tests the case where the only upcoming appointment is Cancelled and the result is null (S-2 AC4).

Most assertions check observable results: toEqual on {id, starts_at, doctor_name}, href and textContent. Some are still weak: toMatchObject on id only, and web REQ-3 uses toContain for the doctor name with a fixture that cannot tell the sources apart.

Covered: the exactly-now boundary, already-started, all-started null, Cancelled/Completed/No-show, local vs UTC date, no appointments, 404, and a clock that moves between reads. The only-Cancelled-upcoming null case is still missing at the API.
API tests use Vitest and Supertest in api/test, on a fresh PG with a fixed clock. Web tests use jsdom and Testing Library in web/src/__tests__. Every name starts with HMS-15 REQ-n or EP-n.
The artifact gives no test counts or coverage numbers. It defers to the verifier, and checks.json shows coverage as skip (exit 78), which matches the artifact.

findings.text: ut.md says the REQ-10 test proves one this.clock() read per request (C5). But PatientService.get also reads the clock through this.today(). The test proves only that appointments and next_appointment share one instant. It passes because today() uses up the 09:29 read.

cites.quote: which proves one read of `this.clock()` per request (C5)

findings.suggested_fix: Reword C5 and the REQ-10 bullet to say that appointments and next_appointment use one shared clock instant, as impl C3 says, not one clock read per request.

cites.quote: API tests use Vitest and Supertest against a throwaway PostgreSQL 16 with a fixed clock.
it('HMS-15 REQ-10: appointments and next_appointment agree even when the clock moves between reads'
Fixed "now" for every test: Monday 19 October 2026, 08:00 in Asia/Kolkata.
The repository gains `nextAppointment(id, now)`, which runs the shared next-appointment SQL for one patient.
The service reads `this.clock()` once and passes that instant to both appointments and nextAppointment.
The verifier skips coverage (the project has no coverage script), so no run reports coverage.
